data.content_ref: inline:Abandon the single fixed point in favor of a set of admissible fixed points and define acceptance as membership in all of them (skeptical intersection), but compute it with alternating graph reachability: a node is accepted iff every maximal admissible set contains it, which is equivalent to the node being in the grounded extension by a known duality. This strengthens the semantics by making it robust to arbitrary changes in the attack graph and gives a natural proof of reinstatement as a set-inclusion property; complexity remains polynomial because admissible sets form an antimatroid and membership can be decided by two reachability queries. Criticism: the equivalence may rely on assumptions about finite graphs that do not hold for dynamic warrant generation.
